# jamfplatform_pro_smart_mobile_device_group (Data Source)

Use this only when the group must belong to a Jamf Pro site. For everything else prefer `jamfplatform_device_group` with `device_type = "mobile"` and `group_type = "smart"`, which manages the same mobile device group across Jamf Platform and is the supported path; it has no site attribute, which is the one thing this adds. Looks one group up by `id` or by exact `name`; supply exactly one. A name match is exact and case-sensitive, so two groups differing only in case resolve separately.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Jamf lists this under **Platform environment** scope (preferred for new integrations) or **Tenant** scope. You choose an integration's scope when you create it in Jamf Account, and cannot change it afterwards. The provider names the scopes it accepts when you configure it, and for a few families that is wider than Jamf lists here. Grant the API integration the following permissions in Jamf Account — see [Getting started with the Platform API](https://developer.jamf.com/platform-api/reference/getting-started-with-platform-api). `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory | Device groups | Read | `device-groups` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look one group up by the identifier Jamf Pro assigned to it.
data "jamfplatform_pro_smart_mobile_device_group" "by_id" {
  id = "19"
}

# Or by display name, matched exactly.
data "jamfplatform_pro_smart_mobile_device_group" "by_name" {
  name = "Supervised iPads"
}

# The criteria come back in evaluation order, which makes this a convenient way
# to read an existing group before bringing it under management.
output "supervised_ipads_criteria" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_smart_mobile_device_group.by_name.criteria
}

# Scope a Jamf Platform construct to the group without importing it.
output "supervised_ipads_platform_id" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_smart_mobile_device_group.by_name.platform_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Jamf Pro identifier for the group. Mutually exclusive with `name`.
- `name` (String) Group display name, matched exactly. Mutually exclusive with `id`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `criteria` (Attributes List) Criteria Jamf Pro evaluates to decide membership, in evaluation order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--criteria))
- `description` (String) Free-text note stored with the group.
- `platform_id` (String) Identifier for this group across Jamf Platform, which is how a blueprint or a compliance benchmark targets it.
- `site_id` (String) Jamf Pro site the group belongs to. `-1` means no site.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--criteria"></a>
### Nested Schema for `criteria`

Read-Only:

- `and_or` (String) How this criterion joins the one before it. The first criterion's value is never used.
- `has_closing_parenthesis` (Boolean) Whether the criterion closes a parenthetical group.
- `has_opening_parenthesis` (Boolean) Whether the criterion opens a parenthetical group.
- `name` (String) Inventory attribute the criterion evaluates.
- `priority` (Number) The criterion's position in the evaluation order.
- `search_type` (String) Comparison the criterion applies.
- `value` (String) Value the criterion compares against.
